story.title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to Resign Following Ethics Committee Findings of Sexual Misconduct
story.summary: Representative Jimmy Gomez has announced his resignation effective December 1 after a House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence of sexual misconduct, including unwanted sexual advances towards a staffer. Gomez disputed the allegations but stated that he felt he had no choice but to resign.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the Ethics finding matter beyond Gomez?
explore_lenses.title: House rules treat power imbalance as central
explore_lenses.summary: The report frames the case as a workplace-safety and institutional-accountability issue, not solely a private-conduct matter. It says a member’s status can make staff interactions coercive even when the staffer is not employed by that member’s own office.

claims.text: The committee found that Gomez violated House Code clauses 1 and 18(b) by making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer, while disregarding the power imbalance between a member and staff.
Clause 18(b) covers unwelcome advances toward House employees, including staff outside a member’s own office; the committee says that scope reflects workplace power dynamics.
The committee said the conduct contributed to the staffer’s departure from House employment and made the congressional workplace more toxic and less safe.

explore_lenses.label: How did the investigation reach this finding?
explore_lenses.title: A public allegation led to a formal inquiry
explore_lenses.summary: The inquiry began after April reporting about Gomez and a congressional staffer, then developed through disclosures, witness testimony and Gomez’s own testimony. Gomez maintained that the encounters were consensual; the committee found the staffer’s account sufficiently credible and rejected that conclusion.

claims.text: The committee says it opened a Rule 18(a) investigation on April 23, 2026, after public reporting that Gomez had been seen kissing a congressional staffer at a 2023 party.

Gomez, through counsel and later in testimony, characterized the relevant contact as consensual; the staffer told the committee there had been more than one physical encounter and that they were not consensual.
The committee found substantial evidence of unwanted advances on two occasions, including sexual contact in public and a forceful encounter in Gomez’s congressional office.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The Ethics Committee’s finding is a House-rules determination, not a criminal conviction. The report says the conduct could implicate D.C. misdemeanor sexual-abuse law, but it does not announce a criminal referral or prosecution.

explore_lenses.label: What happens to the seat and the ethics case now?
explore_lenses.title: The district may be vacant only briefly
explore_lenses.summary: Gomez’s resignation is set for December 1, shortly before the current Congress ends. Because the vacancy would arise after the nomination period closed in the final year of the term, California law gives the governor discretion over whether to call a special election.

claims.text: The committee said Gomez’s defeat in the 2026 election left insufficient time to pursue an adequate House sanction, but that publishing the report would allow the House to consider action while he remains a member.
California law permits, but does not require, the governor to call a special election when a congressional vacancy occurs after the nomination period has closed in the final year of a term.

Forecast: A special election is unlikely to fill the remaining weeks of this term, because a regular vacancy election ordinarily occurs 126 to 140 days after the governor’s proclamation and the next representative was already chosen on November 3; this is an inference from the election timetable and vacancy law, not an announced state decision.

story_report.summary: Rep. Jimmy Gomez is set to resign effective Dec. 1 after the House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence that he made unwanted sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer. The committee concluded that the conduct violated House rules governing member behavior and unwelcome advances toward House employees. Gomez disputed the account, characterizing the relevant contact as consensual, while the staffer told investigators the physical encounters were not consensual.

sections.heading: Ethics Committee Details Gomez Findings
sections.body: The committee opened its investigation on April 23, 2026, following public reporting that Gomez had been seen kissing a congressional staffer at a 2023 party. It found substantial evidence of unwanted advances on two occasions, including sexual contact in public and a forceful encounter in Gomez’s congressional office. The panel said Gomez disregarded the power imbalance between a member of Congress and a staffer.

sections.heading: Gomez Conduct Affected House Staffer
sections.body: The committee concluded that Gomez violated House Code clauses 1 and 18(b), which covers unwelcome advances toward House employees, including staff outside a member’s own office. It said the conduct contributed to the staffer’s departure from House employment and made the congressional workplace more toxic and less safe. The committee said Gomez’s 2026 election defeat left insufficient time to pursue an adequate House sanction, though the report’s release allows the House to consider action while he remains a member.

sections.heading: California Vacancy Process Remains Unset
sections.body: California law permits, but does not require, the governor to call a special election for a congressional vacancy occurring after the nomination period closes in the final year of a term. No gubernatorial proclamation or special-election schedule had been identified as of Nov. 24, 2026. A special election is unlikely to fill the remaining weeks of the term, based on the statutory timetable and the fact that the next representative had already been chosen Nov. 3; that assessment is an inference, not an announced state decision.

unresolved.text: It remains unannounced whether the governor will call a special election for the remaining portion of Gomez’s term.
The ethics finding is not a criminal conviction, and the report did not announce a criminal referral or prosecution despite stating that the conduct could implicate D.C. misdemeanor sexual-abuse law.

related_stories.summary: Choi Kyo-jin, South Korea's education minister, has stepped down following backlash over last-minute security measures aimed at preventing AI-assisted cheating during the college entrance exam. related_stories.title: Reactions to Jensen Huang's Reinstatement at Nvidia Amid Controversy

related_stories.title: India Commits $1.6 Billion in Flood Relief to Nepal During Prime Minister's Visit
related_stories.summary: India has pledged $1.6 billion in flood relief to Nepal as Prime Minister Balendra Shah visits New Delhi. This marks Shah's first international trip since taking office in March. The visit also resulted in agreements on infrastructure projects, including a railway and a hydropower plant.
